title: Elastic memory corridors: quantile-based safety net for KV & activations
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Problem: tenant bursts and long-tail sequences cause sudden KV + activation pressure that either triggers aggressive weight eviction or causes tail latency SLO violations. Existing static reserves (soft watermarks) are inflexible across model families and traffic shapes. Goal: build an elastic, quantile-driven headroom system — "elastic memory corridors" — that dynamically budgets GPU memory across weights, KV, and activations using per-model percentile forecasts and a safety-net eviction policy that minimizes quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Implement per-model quantile estimator that predicts 50/90/99th percentiles of concurrent KV+activation demand over a 30s horizon
Expose an allocator that maintains an upper and lower corridor for each memory class (weights, KV, activations) and enforces a soft-eviction policy when usage crosses the upper corridor
Demonstrate reduction in tail OOM incidents by >= 75% on synthetic tenant-burst tests compared to baseline static reserves
Show less than 10% increase in median latency and graceful degradation (fallback to lower quality model or quantized variant) on overload experiments
Telemetry: new dashboards for corridor fill, eviction counts, predictive error (forecast vs actual), and per-tenant degradation actions
tasks: Design quantile estimator API (histogram reservoir + exponential decay) and choose aggregation cadence (default 5s)
Add telemetry hooks to sample per-request KV & activation footprints (sample rate 1%)
Implement corridor allocator module in runtime that computes lower/upper watermarks from quantiles and current free memory
Implement soft-eviction policy: async KV compaction, graceful activation offload to host pinned memory, and model fallback trigger
Integrate corridor decisions with scheduler: admission control and request tagging for degraded-mode routing
Unit + integration tests: simulator for burst patterns and long-sequence tails
Dashboard and alerts: create Grafana panels and set SLO-linked alert thresholds
Run canary on dedicated pool with 10% traffic and run load tests against multi-tenant workload
design_notes: We chose quantiles over mean because heavy-tailed tenant behavior produces catastrophic outliers; Q90 and Q99 give better headroom signals
Estimator uses reservoired histograms per model-version and a global decay factor so that sudden changes are learned within ~60s while smoothing noise
Corridor computation: lower = Q50 + base_safety (A bytes), upper = Q99 + burst_margin (B bytes) where base_safety and burst_margin are tunable per-tier

Soft-eviction ordering: 1) background KV compaction within same model-version, 2) async activation streaming to host with prefetch hints, 3) quantized-weight switch (if available), 4) degrade to stateless fallback model endpoint
We avoid hard preemption of another tenant's activations; instead we prefer per-tenant transient degradation and admission-control backpressure
Estimator and allocator are implemented as independent services so we can A/B different forecasting algorithms (ARIMA-lite, EWMA-histogram, LSTM in research branch)
tradeoffs: Pros: adaptive headroom reduces wasted reserved memory and reduces OOM incidents; per-model corridors let us tune for model morphologies
Cons: additional telemetry increases memory/profile overhead and CPU for forecasting; complexity in operational tooling and debugging
Quality impact: fallback/quantized paths may reduce output quality — we will tie degradations to automatic QA prompts to detect unacceptable regressions
Risk of oscillation if corridor parameters are too tight; mitigation: add hysteresis and minimal hold times (default 30s)
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): unit tests and local simulator
Stage 2 (canary): enable on dedicated pool subset (10%) + synthetic burst tests for 72h
Stage 3 (gradual ramp): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with continuous monitoring
Post-rollout: 1-week burn-in with daily review and tuning session
monitoring: SLOs: tail-99 latency and successful completion rate; trigger audible alert if OOM incidents increase or degrade actions exceed threshold
Alert: forecast_error_ratio > 2x for 30m => mark estimator unhealthy and fallback to conservative static reserves
